context: Today's selling broke down and then RECOVERED, without crossing the higher point or the round number. The session therefore leaves one question open -- which side it trapped -- and SENSEX has its expiry tomorrow.
plan: SAME CONDITIONAL SHAPE AS YESTERDAY, DIFFERENT REASON: gap up -> BUY, flat or gap down -> SELL, stated for all three indices. The question underneath is WHICH crowd today trapped, and the open is what answers it.

FLAT OR GAP DOWN -> SELL, because the sellers were only TRAPPED and never seated: 'seeing the retracement, who comes here? SELLERS come. But because the market stays SIDEWAYS they leave again' -- so no seller crowd is left to squeeze.

GAP UP -> BUY, the tell is what price did NOT do: 'it did not cross the round number, it did not cross its high point', so 'maybe some good trader slowly bought here and other people could not buy'. That thin long inventory is the target.

THE UNCROSSED HIGH IS WHY RETAIL IS ABSENT: 'because the higher point was not crossed, retail did not do much work'. Only a deliberate buyer may be seated, never a crowd, which is why the buy branch needs the gap up to confirm one exists.
SENSEX EXPIRES TOMORROW, flagged twice -- in his opening line and again at its levels. That is context for the triple-index read, not a premise of its own.
